strap: A daily dispatch from the world you are entering

lead.title: Forty three yachts delivered this year gather in one harbour, and Port Hercule becomes the shortest route to a boat that already exists
lead.standfirst: The Monaco Yacht Show publishes the fleet for its 35th edition, and the composition of that fleet says more about the market than any order book.
lead.body:
The Monaco Yacht Show runs from 23 to 26 September at Port Hercule, and the organisers expect the fleet to reach around 120 superyachts by opening day. Forty three of them were delivered during 2026. That single number is the story of the show. Build slots at the leading yards are now committed through 2028 and 2029, which means a family that decides today to commission a new yacht is discussing a handover three years away. A yacht delivered this year, floating and crewed and available to view for four days in one harbour, has become one of the scarcer commodities in the market.

The 2026 class spans the whole length of the fleet, from the 23.98 metre Arcadia A80 to the 102 metre Lurssen Nixie. The densest bracket sits between 40 and 60 metres, where semi custom series production meets charter economics: Benetti, Riva, Overmarine, Baglietto, Tankoa, Gulf Craft and Sirena Marine all deliver into that band this year. Below 30 metres the picture is almost entirely a 2026 story, with Wally, Princess and Arcadia all fielding new hulls. Italian builders dominate the count, consistent with a global order book in which Italian yards account for 52 per cent of projects ordered or under construction.

The more instructive figure is the brokerage fleet. As of publication, 38 of the confirmed yachts are presented not by the yards that built them but by brokerage and charter houses. Their average length is close to 49 metres and their average launch year is 2016, with hulls running from 27 to 78 metres and launch dates spanning four decades. This is the working fleet, the one that changes hands, charters out, is managed and eventually resold. It is also, in practical terms, the fleet that employs people.

Refit occupies the remaining gap between wanting a yacht and waiting for one. The Feadship Double Haven, launched in 1993 and refitted in 2024, and Benetti's Galaxy, launched in 2005 and refitted in 2025, are both on the quays, brought by resale and repair specialists rather than shipyards. When new tonnage cannot be had before the end of the decade, the refit yard becomes the fastest supplier in the industry, and the calendar of a family's summer starts to be set by a shipyard's availability rather than by the family's own diary.
lead.why: The yachting show week is one of the few moments in the year when the whole logistical chain a private household depends on stands in one place: yards, brokers, managers, captains and crew agencies. Anyone who will one day coordinate a principal's movements between a house and a boat should understand that the boat is now a scarce, scheduled asset, not something summoned at will.

articles.title: Barely two nannies in a hundred will work a rotation, and the households that travel most are hiring from the smallest pool in the profession
articles.body:
Morgan & Mallet's household staff report, drawn from a database of more than 50,300 candidates and placements across the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe and the Middle East, contains one set of figures that explains a great deal about why senior roles now take so long to fill. Only 2.36 per cent of registered nannies work rotational schedules. Only 4.82 per cent travel regularly. Governesses account for 3.71 per cent of registered childcare specialists. The mobile, rotational, multi residence profile that ultra high net worth families increasingly describe as their minimum requirement is held by a very small fraction of the people available to hire.

The same scarcity shows up on the other side of the desk. In France, 21 per cent of client requests over the past year were for domestic couples, and the agency reports that it cannot reliably fill them. In the United States, estate managers represent 10 per cent of requests, and half of all estate manager searches worldwide originate there, a consequence of families holding three to five properties and needing one person who can run at least three of them at once. The skill mix that role demands, security awareness, technical building knowledge and staff management in a single person, is precisely the combination the market has not produced in volume.

Tenure is the third pressure. The report puts average job tenure at roughly three years, against something closer to twenty a generation ago. A household that turns its staff over every three years is permanently in recruitment, and permanently paying the cost of it: the agency now advises families to plan hiring four to six months ahead rather than the traditional two to three, and notes that new staff typically need eight to twelve weeks to become fluent in a household's systems. On those numbers, a single senior departure can consume the better part of a year.

There is a premium attached to the qualities that reduce turnover. Confidentiality and non disclosure compliance are reported to add 15 to 20 per cent to salaries, and candidates who can demonstrate discretion in previous roles typically earn 10 to 15 per cent above market rates. The market is not simply short of people. It is short of people who will move, who will stay, and who can be trusted with what they see.
articles.why: Rotation, travel readiness and a documented record of discretion are the three attributes the data shows to be rarest and best paid. They are also attributes a candidate can decide to build deliberately rather than acquire by accident.
articles.src: Morgan & Mallet International, Household Staff Annual Report

articles.title: Hong Kong counts more than 3,380 single family offices, and the households behind them employ ten thousand people before a single member of staff is hired
articles.body:
A market study commissioned by InvestHK and conducted by Deloitte found that more than 3,380 single family offices were operating in Hong Kong at the end of 2025. That is an increase of roughly 680 offices in two years, growth of more than 25 per cent. The figure matters less as a league table entry than as a measure of how much private wealth has chosen to build permanent administrative infrastructure in one city.

The study estimates that these offices contribute approximately HKD 12.6 billion a year to the local economy through operating expenditure alone, and that they directly employ more than 10,000 full time professionals. That employment figure covers only the office itself: investment staff, legal and compliance, accounting, philanthropy. It does not count the household staff, drivers, chefs and property teams that sit alongside those structures in the same families' lives. Hong Kong's asset and wealth management sector held about HKD 35 trillion, roughly USD 4.5 trillion, at the end of 2024, and the territory ranked second worldwide in the number of ultra high net worth individuals as of June 2025.

The government's ambition is explicit. It has set a target of helping more than 220 family offices establish or expand in Hong Kong between 2026 and 2028, and has signalled legislative proposals to widen the range of qualifying investments for the preferential tax regimes available to funds and single family offices, taking in precious metals, loans and private credit, and digital assets. Single family offices generally require no licence in Hong Kong, a point officials cite as central to the privacy that overseas families value.

For anyone working in private service, the significance is geographic. Each new office represents a family with a reason to spend time in Hong Kong, which in turn means an apartment or house kept ready, a driver on call, schooling arrangements and a calendar that now includes an Asian leg. The administrative decision is taken in a boardroom. The consequences land in a household.
articles.why: Where family offices concentrate, private households follow within a year or two. Tracking these announcements is the most reliable way to anticipate where the next wave of estate and household roles will be posted.
articles.src: Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau and InvestHK, Hong Kong

articles.title: Only a third of family offices have a written succession plan, and the generational transfer has already begun without them
articles.body:
The UBS Global Family Office Report 2026, produced with Campden Wealth, draws on 307 family offices across more than 30 markets with an average net worth of USD 2.7 billion. Among its findings, one stands out for anyone who works inside these families rather than for them: only 35 per cent have a defined succession plan in place. The report frames the coming years as the beginning of a wealth transfer measured in trillions of dollars, moving from one generation to the next, and two thirds of the structures responsible for managing that money have not written down how it will happen.

The investment picture is more decisive than the governance one. Sixty per cent of family offices plan changes to their strategic asset allocation over the next twelve months, and 65 per cent expect confidence in the US dollar's reserve status to weaken. North America still accounts for the largest share of global portfolios, but many offices intend to diversify their regional exposure, with growing interest in Asia Pacific, Greater China and Western Europe. Long term themes such as artificial intelligence remain in favour, though with greater selectivity than a year ago.

The gap between those two facts, decisiveness about portfolios and hesitancy about people, is the texture of daily life in many private households. A family that is confidently rebalancing across three continents may be entirely unable to say who will make decisions about the houses, the collections and the staff in ten years' time. Succession, in practice, is not a single document. It is a slow renegotiation of authority, and it is felt first by the people who need to know whose instructions to follow.

For a house manager or private assistant, the practical effect is a period in which the next generation begins to appear in the household's decisions before it formally holds them. Standards set by a principal over decades meet children and grandchildren with different expectations of formality, technology, privacy and pace. Households that navigate this well tend to be those where procedures were written down rather than carried in one person's memory.
articles.why: Succession inside a family is also succession inside its household. Written procedures, clear inventories and documented preferences are what allow a house to keep functioning while the family works out who is in charge.

articles.title: American buyers take back more than a quarter of the fine wine market, and a three year correction finishes turning
articles.body:
Liv-ex, the London exchange through which most of the world's fine wine trades between merchants, reported that the market stabilised over the first half of 2026, with American buyers returning in force. United States buyers accounted for 26.9 per cent of purchase value in the second quarter, comfortably above the 2025 average of 20.7 per cent and up from 23.3 per cent in the first quarter. Asian buyers, whose appetite drove much of the previous cycle, took more of a back seat.

The correction that preceded this ran for close to three years. The Liv-ex Fine Wine 1000, the exchange's broadest measure, has risen every month since last August, and the market turned positive in September 2025 after that long decline. The recovery is modest rather than dramatic, but it is broad, showing across the principal benchmarks rather than in one region alone.

What has changed is less the price level than who is setting it. A market in which American demand sets the marginal price behaves differently from one led by Asian collectors: the labels that move, the vintages that are drunk rather than stored, and the cellar management practices that follow all shift with the buyer. Italian wines, in particular Piedmont and Tuscany, have led the recent recovery, which is a meaningful change from a decade in which Bordeaux and Burgundy dictated sentiment.

For a household, this is not a market to trade but a market to understand. Cellars in private houses are usually assembled over decades, insured on valuations that age quickly, and drawn on for dinners where the choice of bottle carries meaning. Knowing that the market has turned, and knowing which regions have led the turn, is part of the cultural fluency that separates someone who fetches a bottle from someone who can advise on one.
articles.why: Cellar valuation, insurance schedules and provenance records sit squarely within the estate manager's remit. A rising market is precisely when out of date valuations become expensive.
articles.src: Liv-ex, reported by The Drinks Business

briefs.b: Henley & Partners forecasts that as many as 165,000 millionaires will relocate across borders during 2026, which would be the largest such movement on record. The firm reports that internationally mobile families increasingly assemble what it calls sovereign portfolios of several residence rights and citizenships rather than making a single country move.
briefs.src: Henley & Partners, Private Wealth Migration Report 2026

briefs.b: Altrata's World Ultra Wealth Report 2026 puts the global ultra high net worth population at an all time high of 556,850 individuals, with combined net worth above USD 63.8 trillion after growth of 14.4 per cent in 2025. The firm forecasts 746,570 individuals by 2030, with Asia growing fastest.

Italy continues to lead the Liv-ex recovery, with Piedmont and Tuscany alternating at the top of the performance tables. Barolo Monfortino Riserva 2005 by Giacomo Conterno has been among the strongest performers of the year, rising 25.2 per cent.

The private jet charter services market was valued at USD 16.38 billion in 2025 and is estimated at USD 17.67 billion in 2026, with forecasts pointing to USD 25.79 billion by 2031. Supply has not expanded at the pace of demand, which is why booking windows for peak dates continue to tighten.
briefs.src: Private Jet Charter Services Industry Report 2026
